relationships.subject: GPR68
relationships.evidence_quote: Repeat application of acidic Krebs buffer (pH 6.5–4.0) elicited a robust increase in colonic afferent activity in tissue from GPR68+/+ mice, which was absent in tissue from GPR68-/- mice

relationships.subject: Ogremorphin
relationships.evidence_quote: pharmacological blockade of GPR68 with the selective GPR68 antagonist, OGM (Figure 9A–B) significantly attenuated the peak afferent response

relationships.subject: Ogerin

key_findings: GPR68 is upregulated in colitic human tissue and enriched in Trpv1+ colonic nociceptors; its deletion or antagonism with Ogremorphin abolishes/attenuates acid-evoked colonic afferent firing, while Ogerin potentiates it.
GPR68 loss does not alter colonic afferent or DRG responses to capsaicin, bradykinin or distension; acid-evoked Ca2+ release in Ca2+-free buffer is Gq/PLC dependent.
